description: Chinese cultivation fantasy with stable realm, technique, sect, artifact, and metaphysical terminology.

style: Natural, polished English fantasy prose that remains faithful to the source.
Preserve technical distinctions among cultivation, martial, social, and metaphysical concepts.
Do not flatten source concepts into generic Western fantasy vocabulary.
terminology_preservation_rules: Use established glossary renderings consistently and resist synonym drift, especially for cultivation realms and stages.
Preserve distinctions among cultivation systems, physiques, bloodlines, spiritual roots, Dao concepts, Laws, Intents, Domains, and Tribulations.
Keep sect, clan, faction, hierarchy, technique, artifact, pill, formation, beast, race, demon, and spirit terminology stable when recurring.

Keep recurring states, dynasties, noble and official titles, political institutions, military ranks and units, divine offices, mythological figures, and mythological species stable without conflating them with cultivation grades or personal names.
Do not admit ordinary weapons, medicine, clothing, food, furniture, mundane objects, or one-off descriptions merely because their category is allowed.
translation_policy.pinyin_preference: Chinese character names normally use consistent romanization or pinyin unless the source clearly uses a translatable title, nickname, epithet, or meaningful alias.
translation_policy.semantic_translation_preference: Prefer readable semantic English for descriptive sects, clans, factions, techniques, realms, artifacts, and similar names when it fits established novel terminology; do not automatically leave institutional names in pinyin.

terminology_distinctions: Noble titles and cultivation grades are separate concept classes; do not normalize one into the other.
Political titles and offices must remain distinct from personal names, aliases, and forms of address.
Divine offices or divine classes must remain distinct from cultivation realms, stages, and grades unless the source explicitly equates them.
Keep recurring state, dynasty, and political-institution terminology internally consistent and preserve source distinctions.
Keep recurring military ranks and named military units stable; reject generic troop descriptions.
Keep mythological proper names and recurring mythological species stable while distinguishing figures from species.
Continue to prioritize cultivation realm, stage, subdivision, and system consistency.

review_priorities: Cultivation realms, stages, and systems must remain distinct and stable.
Character names and aliases normally use consistent romanization.
Noble titles, government or historical offices, political titles, personal names, and cultivation grades must remain distinct.
States, dynasties, political institutions, divine offices, mythological figures, and mythological species require stable renderings when recurring.
Military ranks and named military units require stable renderings when recurring; generic troop descriptions do not belong in the glossary.
Sect, clan, faction, and organization names should be readable and consistent.
Named cultivation, martial, movement, sword, secret, divine, and forbidden techniques require stable renderings.
Artifacts, weapons, treasures, talismans, formations, pills, herbs, and materials enter the glossary only when named or recurring.
Physiques, bloodlines, spiritual roots, constitutions, races, beasts, demons, spirits, and metaphysical terminology retain source distinctions.
Forms of address preserve meaningful family, seniority, sect, and cultivation hierarchy.
Reject mundane objects, ordinary vocabulary, and one-off descriptions.

priorities: Cultivation realm, stage, and system consistency.
Noble-title versus cultivation-grade consistency; do not conflate political status with cultivation rank.
Political-title or office versus personal-name and alias consistency.
Divine-office or divine-class versus cultivation-grade consistency.
Recurring military ranks and named military units.
Mythological proper names and recurring mythological species.
Sect, clan, faction, and organization names.
Cultivation, martial, movement, and sword techniques.
Secret arts, divine abilities, and forbidden techniques.
Artifacts, weapons, treasures, talismans, and formations.
Pills, medicines, spiritual herbs, and special materials.
Physiques, bloodlines, spiritual roots, and constitutions.
Races, beasts, species, demons, and spirits.

Dao concepts, Laws, Intents, Domains, energies, and Tribulations.
